forecaster_note: Surf Guru read: A proper clean winter weekend — a long-period S groundswell is already running (6.4ft @ 11s from 184° today, building to 7.4ft @ 11s from 180° Sunday) with deep-water energy climbing 648 → ~1160 kJ, all under light W-to-WSW offshore each morning. The catch is direction: it's near-dead-S, which wraps soft into Dee Why and is shadowed at Manly, so the size lives at the S-magnets — Long Reef (overhead to 2x overhead) and Curl Curl. Dee Why still rates fair-good off the Point where the swell corners into a clean frontside right. Best all-rounder is Saturday; biggest is Sunday, but an ESE onshore fills the Sunday arvo so surf early. 🦈 SLSNSW cleared Manly / North Steyne after a drone shark sighting around midday yesterday (Fri 24 Jul) — reopened 1:24pm; no detections at Dee Why, Long Reef or Curl Curl in the last 24h.

wind.summary: Light W offshore ~13 km/h through your mid-morning window — clean and groomed, easing to near-glass by early afternoon. Holds W/WSW offshore Sunday morning, then an ESE onshore fills the arvo; dawn-to-midday is the play both days.

shark.summary: SLSNSW drone spotted a shark off Manly / North Steyne around 12:15pm yesterday (Fri 24 Jul) — the beach was cleared and reopened by 1:24pm. No detections at Dee Why, Long Reef or Curl Curl in the last 24h. Stay #SharkSmart at Manly.

days.label: Today
days.note: A proper clean winter morning — solid long-period S groundswell (6.4ft @ 11s from 184°) under light W offshore. The catch is direction: dead-south wraps soft into Dee Why. The size sits at the S-magnets — Long Reef is overhead-plus, Curl Curl chest-to-overhead. Best window is mid-morning around the 10:30am low. ⚠️ Shark cleared Manly/North Steyne yesterday midday — stay sharp there.

swells.label: Primary S groundswell — wraps soft here

dee-why.window: The Point is the play — a wrapping S can hold a long clean right while the open beach stays shadowed. 648 kJ at 11s is real groundswell, but it feeds Dee Why side-on; the light W offshore grooms it. Go mid-morning off the 10:30am low.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: Dead-S 184° wraps weak into Dee Why proper, so set up wide on the Point where it corners into a rippable frontside right. Clean offshore and an 11s period — pick the sets and drive off the bottom turn; it's shape over raw size here.

long-reef.window: Standout of the four — the S-swell magnet turns 184° into overhead-plus faces, sets to 6ft. Light W is close to straight offshore here, so it's the cleanest of the group; earliest is glassiest and a strong paddle is rewarded.

tip.label: Frontside tip
tip.text: This is where the size lives — overhead sets off a solid 11s S groundswell, and the right off the point is your frontside. 648 kJ has real push, so take off deep and it'll run. Step up toward the FMN3 if the sets stack.

curl-curl.window: Second for size behind Long Reef — punchy chest-to-overhead corners off cleaner banks. Best on the pushing low mid-morning under the W offshore.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: More exposed than Dee Why so it grabs the S swell — hunt the banked lefts on your backhand and stay high through the fatter sections. Clean offshore all morning.

alerts: 🦈 SLSNSW drone cleared Manly / North Steyne after a shark sighting ~12:15pm yesterday (Fri 24 Jul); reopened 1:24pm. Check the live map before you paddle out.
manly.window: Smallest and most protected — waist-to-chest, clean under the W offshore. Not worth the drive over Long Reef, and there was a shark clearance here yesterday.

tip.label: Backside tip
tip.text: North Steyne stays small on a dead-S swell — soft, forgiving corners. If you do surf it, keep an eye out after yesterday's drone sighting. Groveller if you just want water time.

days.label: Tomorrow
days.note: Swell builds bigger and even more dead-south — 7.4ft @ 11s from 180°, energy up near 1160 kJ. W/WSW offshore holds the morning before an ESE onshore sea breeze fills the arvo, so surf early. Long Reef jumps to 2x overhead; Dee Why gets a clean chest-to-overhead push at the Point.

dee-why.window: Bigger and cleaner early — chest-to-overhead at the Point on the WSW offshore. Get in before the ESE onshore fills the arvo. Rates fair-good off shape; the open beach stays shadowed by the dead-S angle.

long-reef.window: Cranking — up to 2x overhead at the S magnet. WSW is more cross here so it carries some bump; go at first light for the cleanest faces. The serious session of the weekend — step-up board and respect it.

curl-curl.window: Head-high-plus and punchy — takes the big S far better than Dee Why. Cross-WSW so earliest is smoothest; surf before the arvo onshore.

manly.window: Still the smallest as the swell swings dead-S — mellow but clean early. The manageable option if Long Reef is too much.

days.label: Weekend
days.note: Clean S groundswell both days, building to a Sunday peak (~1160 kJ, 11s). Offshore each morning — dawn-to-midday is the play, with an ESE onshore filling Sunday arvo. Long Reef and Curl Curl hold the size; Dee Why and Manly stay shadowed by the dead-S direction. Best all-rounder is Saturday; biggest is Sunday.

alerts: Near-dead-S swell (180–184°) — big energy on paper but it wraps soft into Dee Why. The Point grooms it into a clean right; the open beach stays well under what the kJ suggests.
dee-why.window: Offshore mornings both days. The Point is the pick — a wrapping S holds a long clean frontside right while the beachies stay shadowed. Shape over size.

long-reef.window: Biggest of the run — solid 2ft-overhead sets peaking Sunday. Cross-SW adds bump; earliest is cleanest. Step-up board — the session of the weekend for confident surfers.

curl-curl.window: Head-high-plus at the peak, punchy on the low. Handles the S swell far better than Dee Why; go early before the wind.

alerts: S swell heavily shadowed by the southern headland — smallest of the four by a wide margin. Note yesterday's shark clearance at North Steyne.
manly.window: Clean but shadowed. Only worth it if the bigger spots are too much, or for an easy paddle.
